component.name: Windows VM Installer
component.summary: Install Windows on another disk, without a USB stick

description.p: Install Windows onto a physical disk from Linux, without a USB stick and without touching firmware settings. The Windows installer runs inside a hidden QEMU/KVM virtual machine that can see only the target disk; when its first phase is done, you reboot into the new disk and Windows finishes the setup on the real hardware.

Your Linux disk is safe: the installer cannot see it, so it cannot erase it or put its boot files on it. Windows gets its own EFI system partition, you pick the edition you are licensed for, and the new system is added to the boot manager you use (Limine, GRUB, rEFInd).
Requires QEMU, OVMF firmware, swtpm and efibootmgr on the host, a Windows 10/11 x64 ISO, and a target disk of at least 64 GB connected through NVMe or SATA. The target disk is erased: keep backups.
Early development: tested on disk image files.
